title: Criminal Procedure
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze the Fourth Amendment (searches, warrants and their exceptions, and the exclusionary rule), the Fifth Amendment (Miranda, self-incrimination and double jeopardy), the Sixth Amendment (counsel, confrontation, jury and speedy trial), identification procedures and due process.
primary_reading: Constitution Annotated: the Fourth, Fifth and Sixth Amendments

weeks.3: Warrant exceptions: exigency, consent and plain view
weeks.4: Vehicles, searches incident to arrest, and stop and frisk
weeks.5: The exclusionary rule and its limits
weeks.6: Standing and the fruit of the poisonous tree
weeks.8: Voluntariness and the right to counsel during questioning
weeks.10: The right to counsel and effective assistance
weeks.12: Jury trial, speedy trial and plea bargaining

blocks.deliverable: Decide whether five police actions are searches.
Apply the warrant exceptions to a vehicle search.
Decide what evidence is suppressed after a supplied arrest.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a custodial interrogation for Miranda violations.
Apply Strickland v. Washington to a defense lawyer's errors.
Analyze a double-jeopardy problem with two prosecutions.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Suppression motion: from a supplied police report and transcript, write a motion to suppress with a supporting memorandum of law, then a short prosecution response.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
